paragraphs: MCM sells software that helps public safety agencies stay ahead of risk, increase safety and maintain compliance by managing assets, certifications, maintenance and inspections in one connected platform. The product is framed as intelligent operational readiness for public safety.

Asset tracking keeps a full lifecycle history from procurement through retirement. Issuance and chain of custody let staff issue serialized assets and consumable inventory in the same transaction. Work orders are created automatically when an inspection fails. Custom templates can be built for any inspection type, including vehicles, weapons, jump bags, respirators, facilities and sites. An open REST API is offered for connecting other systems, and the integrations page claims to be the only platform that integrates directly with major radio manufacturers.

The company cites 300+ public safety agencies nationwide. For fire agencies the aim is to keep apparatus, gear and crew inspection-ready at every station and before the next call comes in. For government and utilities it gives full asset visibility and tracks grant-funded resources. A news post announces Anthony Rotoli as new CEO. Agencies that would rather not administer the system themselves can buy managed services, pitched as maximum impact without the administrative overhead.

quote.text: Don't let gaps in operations become public safety risk.
